Slop PDF · free, in your browser

A free Adobe Acrobat alternative in your browser

If you need to sign, fill, edit or tidy up a PDF now and then, Slop PDF does it in a browser tab: free, with no installation and no account, and your files stay on your device.

Open Slop PDF

Watch the Slop PDF tutorial: a free PDF editor in the browser
On YouTube, about one minute.

How to do it

  1. Open Slop PDF and drop your PDF on the page.
  2. Pick a tool in the rail: Organize, Edit page, Sign, Redact, Page numbers, Watermark, Forms, Compress, Convert or OCR.
  3. Make your changes. Every step can be undone.
  4. Choose Download to save the new PDF.

What Slop PDF does: reorder, rotate, delete, merge and split pages; add text, shapes, pictures, comments and signatures; edit existing text; fill forms; true redaction; page numbers and watermarks; lossless or strong compression; OCR for scans; and export to images, Word, Excel or PowerPoint. Password-protected PDFs open when you know the password.

Your files stay on this device: Slop PDF runs in your browser, with no upload, no account and no watermark.

Questions

Is Slop PDF connected to Adobe?

No. Slopographic is not affiliated with Adobe. Adobe and Acrobat are trademarks of their owner, used here only to describe what people search for.

Do I need to install anything?

No. Slop PDF runs in a current browser on Windows, macOS, Linux, ChromeOS, Android or iOS. You can also download it as a single offline file from the File menu.

Are my PDFs uploaded?

No. Files are opened and saved in your browser and never sent to a server. There is no account to create.

Can it open password-protected PDFs?

Yes, when you know the password: the file is unlocked on your device so it can be edited and saved.
